statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 24, the top of the watch band and one point below the block threshold. NQ futures were verified at 29,061.50, down 387.25 points or 1.31%, holding within about 20 points of a 29,043.25 session low that extended after the 12:30 UTC producer price release from the 29,216.75 low observed before it. E-mini S&P 500 futures were likewise on their session low at 7,599.25, down 0.58%, and the cash session opened lower with QQQ at 707.67, down 1.21%. August producer prices rose 0.4% on the month and 5.4% over twelve months, matching the headline consensus, while the core measures came in at or below expectations and initial claims at 206K were close to forecast. Brent crude trades at 105.30, up 4.04% and at its highest since 19 May, the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.92% and the 2-year 4.52%, both extended since the previous assessment, and VIX is 17.61, up 7.0%. Observed extension to a new session low alongside an aligned yields, oil and volatility stack lifts tail from 20 to the top of the watch band, while an orderly decline, an absolutely low volatility level and a release that was not uniformly hawkish keep it below the block threshold.
recommendation: Tail at 24 maps the policy state to WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, with pause false and caution true under the fixed repository mapping. The narrow evidence-based danger window runs 13:30-15:30 UTC, covering the cash open and the first two cash hours, which is where an already one-way tape, a long end at a three-year high and an oil market near multi-month highs could combine into the shallow-pullback structure that matters for a mean-reversion book. Conditional tail peaks at 26 in the 14:00 UTC hour, the only slot in the window mapped to the block band, and that peak is explicitly conditional on opening-auction continuation that has not yet been observed. Outside the window the conditional path decays through the U.S. afternoon toward an 11 overnight floor, then drifts back up to 22 in the final slot, which contains the August consumer price index at 12:30 UTC on 11 September. Stress remains extreme at 86 because the energy-driven inflation impulse, a European Central Bank that raised rates today and a Federal Reserve decision on 16 September are all unresolved. Stress at that level describes the environment; it does not on its own move the mapped state past the block threshold.
headline: NQ extends to a new 29,043.25 low after in-line August PPI and opens the cash session 1.2% lower; tail rises to 24 at the top of the watch band
body:
The post-release price path that the previous assessment could not yet verify has now been observed, and it extended rather than retraced. NQ futures were verified at 29,061.50, down 387.25 points or 1.31% from a 29,448.75 close, against a session range of 29,043.25 to 29,508.25. Two independent quote sources agree on that level to within four points. The relevant detail is not the size of the decline but its shape: the low observed before the release at 29,216.75 was taken out and extended to 29,043.25, and price is sitting roughly twenty points above it rather than retracing from it. E-mini S&P 500 futures show the same structure at 7,599.25 against a 7,598.00 session low. The cash session then opened lower, with QQQ printing 707.67 at the 13:30 UTC auction, down 1.21%.

The release itself was close to consensus and does not explain the move on its own. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the producer price index for final demand rose 0.4% in August and 5.4% over the twelve months ended in August, with the measure excluding foods, energy and trade services up 0.3% on the month and 4.7% over the year. The headline monthly figure matched the consensus estimate, the narrower core measures came in at or below expectations, and initial jobless claims at 206K against 205K expected carried no labour-market shock. What is driving the tape is the channel behind the headline rather than the print: an energy-led inflation impulse that markets are translating directly into rate expectations.

That channel is coherent across every asset checked. Brent crude trades at 105.30, up 4.04% on the day and at its highest level since 19 May, with the move traced to the seventh month of U.S.-Iran conflict and continued disruption around the Strait of Hormuz. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.92% and the 2-year 4.52%, both up seven to eight basis points on the day and both extended since the previous assessment observed 4.88% and 4.48%; the long end is at its highest in roughly three years. The European Central Bank raised its three key rates by 25 basis points this morning, taking the deposit facility to 2.50% with effect from 16 September, explicitly citing Middle East conflict as a continuing source of inflation pressure. VIX at 17.61 is up 7.0%.

The judgment that keeps this below the block threshold rests on what is absent as much as on what is present. The decline is orderly: roughly 465 points from the Globex high across a full overnight session, with VIX at an absolute level that does not describe a disorderly market. Dispersion is wide rather than uniform, with the E-mini down 0.58% against the Nasdaq contract's 1.31%, which reads as a duration-sensitive de-rating rather than a broad risk-off cascade. The release was not the hawkish shock the pre-market positioning appeared to anticipate. And the single most decisive piece of evidence, whether the opening auction extends the trend, is about one minute old at assessment time and cannot yet be scored. Tail therefore sits at 24, the top of the watch band, rather than in the block band.

The forward path places the conditional peak at 26 in the 14:00 UTC hour, the first full cash hour, which is the point at which a no-retracement structure would have to establish itself if it is going to. That single slot maps to the block band. Conditional tail then decays through the afternoon, ticks up for the power hour where closing-auction flow can extend a directional day, and reaches an 11 floor overnight. It climbs back gradually through the European morning to 22 in the final slot, which contains the August consumer price index at 12:30 UTC on 11 September. That anticipatory climb is deliberately gentle and is expressed mainly through stress and falling confidence, because a scheduled release is a checkpoint and not an observed price path. Stress stays extreme for most of the window and troughs at 75 overnight without any underlying driver resolving.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 13:00 UTC on 9 September to 12:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 17 in the 13:00 UTC slot on 9 September, dips to 10 in the following hour, ticks to 16 in the 15:00 UTC hour on an event/whipsaw read, and then settles into a 13 to 9 band across the U.S. close and the overnight session. The Asian and early European hours of 10 September held a narrow 8 to 11 range with a mixed dominant mode and confidence steady at 87 to 88. The last two slots mark the turn: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC with the dominant mode switching to trend-down as the pre-release grind became directional, then tail 20 at 12:00 UTC with the mapped state at WATCH and the mode read as event/whipsaw around the producer price release. Stress never left the extreme band across the whole window, ranging from 80 to 85, which is the clearest signal that a difficult high-volatility environment has coexisted with a tail score that stayed below the block threshold for the entire 24 hours. Past assessments are reported as they were published and are not revised using later information.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from a producer price release that has already printed to a consumer price release that lands inside the final slot. Conditional tail peaks at 26 in the 14:00 UTC hour, the first full cash hour and the only slot in the window mapped to the block band, then eases to 24 and 21 as the danger window closes at 15:30 UTC. It decays through the U.S. afternoon to 16, ticks back to 18 for the power hour where closing-auction flow can extend a directional day, and reaches an 11 floor across the Asian session. From the European pre-open it climbs one point per hour through 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 to 19 in the hour before the August consumer price index, then 22 in the 12:00 UTC slot that contains the 12:30 UTC release. That anticipatory climb deliberately raises stress and lowers confidence more than it raises tail, because hypothetical post-event alignment is not treated as observed structure. Stress runs from 86 in the cash-open hours down to a 75 overnight trough and back to 85 in the release slot. Confidence falls from 87 to 69 across the window, reflecting how much of the forward path depends on price structure that has not yet formed. Beyond the window, the Federal Reserve decision, projections and press conference on 16 September remain the dominant scheduled risk.
